summary: The former Blizzard developer has moved on.
body: Despite some big changes happening with Overwatch lately, former game director Jeff Kaplan hasn't touched it since the year he left Blizzard. In fact, he actively avoids the game in every way he can, he told GameSpot in a recent interview. Before Overwatch, Kaplan rose through the ranks on the World of Warcraft team, starting in QA and eventually becoming game director. He described his departure from the WoW team in 2008 as "a training moment" for when he would leave the Overwatch team, and Blizzard altogether, in 2021. "I kind of went through a little bit of shock leaving WoW back in 2008," Kaplan says. "So, when I stepped away from Overwatch in April of 2021, I was kind of used to that moment of what it meant to give all of yourself, your heart, your soul–because it's not just a job, there's no one who can do this and have it just be a job–and then have this shocking moment where you realize it doesn't belong to you. It belongs to the team, belongs to the players, it belongs to Blizzard, but it doesn’t belong to you." A few minutes of troubleshooting later, I deduced that the game wouldn't display on a monitor with its refresh rate set higher than 120 Hz. Easily solved, but I kept thinking of that quirk when I selected the in-game 120 fps cap and then watched the game jarringly lurch down to a lower framerate every time I hit a cutscene. Maybe these technical quirks were treats for reviewers that have been smoothed over in time for launch. They haven't stopped me from having a lot of fun with the eight or so hours I've played Belmont's Curse—I think I'm closing in on the halfway point, and it keeps getting better as it goes. body: More radical changes beyond just giving the characters necks are coming to Garry's Mod successor s&box . Facepunch Studios' game creation platform's launch in April was met with a swarm of negative reviews, complaints of AI slop filling its user-generated game collection, and swiftly plummeting user numbers. Now creator Garry Newman is reversing course on some of his decisions, such as pivoting to a 'greenlight type system' for user-generated games and announcing that the platform is going free to play much earlier than expected. "Our focus has been on the engine and the development experience. That’s what we love, that’s what turns us on—but we’re not selling an engine, we’re selling a game," Newman wrote this week. "So we need to do much much better on the game, we need to shift our focus to what players are experiencing, not developers." That focus, Newman said, will be on improving the sandbox mode for players by adding more NPCs, vehicles, and customization. "I’ve let everyone down that was expecting that. title: Ace Combat Zero gets its own standalone app on Steam, freeing it from the 136GB install of Ace Combat 8
summary: The biggest complaint about the pre-order bonus game is getting resolved with a happy ending.
body: Ace Combat 8 rocks. PC Gamer's reviewer scored it a 92% , and I've been savoring the campaign, because I know it could be years until we get another bombastic flight sim melodrama of its kind. Although I do have another Ace Combat lined up to play after: Ace Combat Zero, which was included as a free pre-order bonus with AC8, and subsequently responsible for the majority of the new game's negative launch day reviews. Not because Zero is bad—it's a series fan-favorite—but because Bandai Namco inexplicably bundled it into the AC8 launcher, meaning you can't download this 3.2GB port of a 2006 PS2 game without the 136 gigabytes of Wings of Theve. This decision was not well received . body: Dan Houser is a co-founder of Rockstar Games and so I would never presume to tell him he's wrong about any of the games Rockstar has made— except in this one particular instance, where I feel obligated to step up and say, 'Dan, I'm sorry bud, but you're wrong.' The game in question is Max Payne 3 , on which Houser played a central role, and one he seems rather down on: In an interview with IGN , he said the game was a "failure" because, simply put, he's not Sam Lake, the Remedy creative director who wrote the first two Max Payne games. As a very linear game, Max Payne 3 "was a little different" from the open world GTA games he was accustomed to, Houser said, but he also really enjoyed the experience. title: World of Warcraft: Forever won't destroy what made the old classes so satisfying by modernizing them into oblivion: 'The level of mechanical complexity found in the beta classes is indicative of our intentions'
summary: You will wait patiently for your next ability and you will learn to love it.
body: Part of World of Warcraft: Forever's charm is that combat is considerably slower than the regular version of the MMO. It's the kind of game where you'll spend 38 seconds hitting a scorpion because there are so few buttons to press in the early stages of your journey. Classes in WoW's past were simple, but had small quirks to them that you'd pick up over time. Melee classes, for example, can squeeze abilities in between their auto attacks to maximize their damage output. You'd never care about this if fights only took 10 seconds, like they do in WoW today, but back then you had to use all that time in more drawn-out battles for something . The WoW: Forever beta has reminded me how satisfying it is to play a class that isn't built like Whac-A-Mole, where the challenge is to hit the right buttons the moment they start to glow. There's a rhythm to WoW's old classes and I'm delighted to hear that Blizzard fully intends to maintain it in WoW: Forever. Blizzard developers told TechRadar that they want "to err on the side of simpler classes, but with engaging depth," and that all of it will align with its guiding principle of staying true to the old MMO's "core design, pacing, and tone." …

title: How to equip ambers in Valor Mortis
summary: Slot these rare gems to gain passive bonuses and abilities.
body: (Image credit: One More Level) Key deets 💎 Ambers are precious gems you equip to gain passive bonuses and abilities. 💎 You can slot them at the level up menu with any lantern. 💎 You unlock a new slot every ten levels. You'll most likely find your first amber in Valor Mortis before you're actually able to equip it. The game has a fairly simplistic skill tree that focuses around passive buffs, so the ambers you equip are more what add a bit of spice to your build. You can equip an amber once you reach Level 5 by leveling up at any lantern. When you enter the level up menu, you'll notice that a slot with a + symbol has unlocked on the bottom layer—click on this and select the amber you want to equip, and don't worry, you can swap them at any time. After this, you'll unlock a new slots every ten levels at: Slot two : Level 15 Slot three : Level 25 Slot four : Level 35 Slot five : Level 45 This means there are five amber slots overall. You'll generally get new ambers from quests and chests, and any amber you already own will level up to provide a more powerful passive bonus when you acquire a copy of it.
